mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS trend and 20d SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the positive return rate is not significantly higher than baseline (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% over a 3-month period signals a weakening labor market that may lead to a recession, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 5.0% year-over-year), a further increase in inflation signals the Federal Reserve will tighten policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 30% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 5.0% yoy.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening consumer confidence and economic activity, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is active in all economic regimes.
failure_condition: The positive correlation between HOUST trend and 20d SPX returns falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 (index, 2017=100) for two consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 95.0 for 2 months fails to predict negative 5d returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which is a strong predictor of negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of UNRATE rising and PAYEMS falling fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5% per annum, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 35% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.
